questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The courses offered by the university and what they contained.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: There was a information meeting on Zoom where we were told everything we needed to know. So it was quite easy to get started in the city and at the university.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The tartuwelcomecentre was very useful for getting started.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
I used
hugo.stay
. It is quite easy, but a little expensive considering what you get. I would recommend it.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Everything is within a 10 minute walk if you live anywhere near the center, so it doesn't really matter where you live. I recommend the dorms however, if you like being social and partying.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Exchange students had limited options through the university.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I just got some logins to their systems, signed up for courses and showed up to the courses. It was very easy.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I didn't seek out help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Few of the classes I initially wanted were available, but I found some other courses that were very interesting. I couldn't sign up for them myself however, since they were master courses and I was registered as a bachelor. I was able to fix this after sending a few mails however.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It is very easy. I don't know what else to say.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The workload is higher, but in general it is also much easier. I wish I was challenged some more.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: All my courses were master courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was lot more practical and personal. I had a much closer bond with the professors here than at my home university. I do however prefer the content of the courses at UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MTAT.03.227	Machine Learning
MTAT.07.017	Applied Cryptography
MTAT.08.020	Parallel Computing
MTAT.03.319	Business Data Analytics
LTAT.06.012	Autonomous Vehicles Project

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
MTAT.07.017	Applied Cryptography
is a very good course, but it is also known for being hard. I don't think it is very hard if you know a little programming, but I can see why people would consider it to be challenging.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: A lot of public transportation is free. I didn't need any books for any of my courses.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I don't know, I didn't look much into it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Join the ESN activities, they are a lot of fun.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: There is plenty to see in both Tartu and Tallinn.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: A lot of old people don't speak English, but luckily Tartu is filled with mostly young people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: They are quite nice, just talk to them

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really liked how it felt doing christmas.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: I only have one thing. When I went on exchange, the thing I worried about the most was all the things I was going to miss out on, and how everything will have changed once I come back. You will experience so many much more amazing things while on exchange, and when you come back, you will realize the only thing that has changed is you.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: I met a lot of nice people, and got to experience what it was like to study at another place.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: It can be quite expensive, and lonely at times, being away from the people you know can be hard, but luckily you make a lot of new friends while on exchange.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
